API Reference BEN2 - Background Erase Network On this page BEN2 - Background Erase Network BEN2 (Background Erase Network 2) is a state-of-the-art background removal model integrated into OpenTryOn. It provides high-quality background removal for fashion and product images, making it ideal for e-commerce, virtual try-on preprocessing, and product photography. Overview​ BEN2 uses a transformer-based architecture with window attention mechanisms for precise foreground-background separation. The model automatically downloads weights from Hugging Face on first use. Key Features​ High Precision: State-of-the-art accuracy for background removal Automatic Weight Download: Weights automatically downloaded from Hugging Face Foreground Refinement: Optional refinement for higher quality edges Batch Processing: Process multiple images efficiently Flexible Input: Accepts file paths, URLs, bytes, base64 (Studio/MCP uploads), BytesIO, or PIL Images GPU Acceleration: CUDA support for faster processing Requirements​ CUDA 11.8+ (recommended for GPU acceleration) PyTorch 2.1+ Model weights are automatically cached after first download Installation​ BEN2 is included with OpenTryOn. The model weights are automatically downloaded on first use: pip install opentryon Quick Start​ Single Image​ from tryon.api.ben2 import BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapterfrom PIL import Image# Initialize adapter (weights download automatically on first use)adapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter()# Remove background from a single imageresult = adapter.remove_background("model.jpg")# Save the result (PNG with transparency)result[0].save("model_no_bg.png") Batch Processing​ from tryon.api.ben2 import BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapteradapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter()# Process multiple imagesimages = ["model1.jpg", "model2.jpg", "model3.jpg"]results = adapter.remove_background_batch(images)# Save all resultsfor i, img in enumerate(results): img.save(f"output_{i+1}.png") Command Line Usage​ Use the unified opentryon CLI (the old root bg_remove.py wrapper was removed in v0.0.7): # Single image background removal (saved under outputs/)opentryon bg-remove --model ben2 --image model.jpg# Choose the output directoryopentryon bg-remove --model ben2 --image model.jpg --output-dir results# With foreground refinement for higher qualityopentryon bg-remove --model ben2 --image model.jpg --refine# Several images: loop in your shell (the CLI processes one image per call)for f in model_1.jpg model_2.jpg model_3.jpg; do opentryon bg-remove --model ben2 --image "$f" --refine --output-dir resultsdone For in-process batches use remove_background_batch from the Python API below. A hosted alternative is --model fashn-bg-remove (FASHN_API_KEY, 1 credit per image). CLI Arguments​ Argument Type Default Description --model string - ben2 (local) or fashn-bg-remove (hosted) --image, -i string - Image path or URL (required) --refine flag False Enable foreground refinement (ben2 only) --output-dir, -o string outputs Output directory for results --dry-run flag False Print the resolved call without running it Python API​ BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter​ The main adapter class for background removal. Constructor​ BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter( weights_path: str = None, # Custom weights path (optional) device: str = None # Device: "cuda" or "cpu" (auto-detected)) Methods​ remove_background​ Remove background from a single image. def remove_background( self, image: Union[str, io.BytesIO, Image.Image], refine: bool = False) -> List[Image.Image] Parameters: image: Input image (file path, URL, BytesIO, or PIL Image) refine: Enable foreground refinement for higher quality edges Returns: List containing a single PIL Image with transparent background Example: adapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter()# From file pathresult = adapter.remove_background("model.jpg")# From URLresult = adapter.remove_background("https://example.com/model.jpg")# From PIL Imagefrom PIL import Imageimg = Image.open("model.jpg")result = adapter.remove_background(img)# With refinementresult = adapter.remove_background("model.jpg", refine=True)# Save resultresult[0].save("output.png") remove_background_batch​ Remove background from multiple images. def remove_background_batch( self, images: List[Union[str, io.BytesIO, Image.Image]], refine: bool = False) -> List[Image.Image] Parameters: images: List of input images (file paths, URLs, BytesIO, or PIL Images) refine: Enable foreground refinement for all images Returns: List of PIL Images with transparent backgrounds Example: adapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter()# Process multiple imagesimages = [ "model1.jpg", "model2.jpg", "https://example.com/model3.jpg"]results = adapter.remove_background_batch(images, refine=True)# Save all resultsfor i, img in enumerate(results): img.save(f"output_{i+1}.png")print(f"Processed {len(results)} images") load_image​ Load and normalize image from various input formats. def load_image( self, input_data: Union[str, io.BytesIO, Image.Image]) -> Image.Image Supported Inputs: File paths (local files) URLs (http/https) BytesIO / file-like objects PIL Image objects Use Cases​ Virtual Try-On Preprocessing​ Remove backgrounds from garment images before virtual try-on: from tryon.api.ben2 import BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapterfrom tryon.api import KlingAIVTONAdapter# Step 1: Remove garment backgroundbg_adapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter()garment_clean = bg_adapter.remove_background("garment.jpg", refine=True)garment_clean[0].save("garment_clean.png")# Step 2: Use cleaned garment for virtual try-onvton_adapter = KlingAIVTONAdapter()result = vton_adapter.generate_and_decode( source_image="model.jpg", reference_image="garment_clean.png") E-Commerce Product Photos​ Create professional product photos with transparent backgrounds: from tryon.api.ben2 import BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapterfrom pathlib import Pathadapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter()# Process all product images in a folderinput_dir = Path("raw_products")output_dir = Path("processed_products")output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)images = list(input_dir.glob("*.jpg"))results = adapter.remove_background_batch([str(img) for img in images], refine=True)for img_path, result in zip(images, results): output_path = output_dir / f"{img_path.stem}.png" result.save(output_path) print(f"Processed: {output_path}") Model Swap Preprocessing​ Prepare images for model swapping: from tryon.api.ben2 import BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapteradapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter()# Remove background for cleaner model swapperson_clean = adapter.remove_background("person.jpg", refine=True)person_clean[0].save("person_clean.png") Performance Tips​ GPU Acceleration​ BEN2 automatically uses CUDA if available: import torch# Check if CUDA is availableprint(f"CUDA available: {torch.cuda.is_available()}")# BEN2 will automatically use GPU if availableadapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter() # Auto-detects device# Or explicitly set deviceadapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter(device="cuda") # Force GPUadapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter(device="cpu") # Force CPU Batch Processing​ For multiple images, batch processing is more efficient: # Less efficient: processing one by onefor img in images: result = adapter.remove_background(img) # process result...# More efficient: batch processingresults = adapter.remove_background_batch(images)for result in results: # process results... Refinement Trade-offs​ The refine parameter improves edge quality but increases processing time: # Fast processing (no refinement)result = adapter.remove_background("image.jpg", refine=False)# Higher quality (with refinement) - takes longerresult = adapter.remove_background("image.jpg", refine=True) Model Architecture​ BEN2 uses a Swin Transformer-based architecture with: Window Attention: Efficient self-attention in local windows Shifted Windows: Cross-window connections for global context Multi-scale Processing: Captures both fine details and global structure Foreground Refinement: Optional post-processing for cleaner edges The model weights are downloaded from Hugging Face: PramaLLC/BEN2. Troubleshooting​ Common Issues​ CUDA Out of Memory​ For large images on limited GPU memory: # Use CPU insteadadapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter(device="cpu")# Or resize images before processingfrom PIL import Imageimg = Image.open("large_image.jpg")img.thumbnail((2048, 2048)) # Resize to max 2048pxresult = adapter.remove_background(img) Weights Download Issues​ If automatic download fails: # Manually download weightsimport huggingface_hubhuggingface_hub.hf_hub_download( repo_id="PramaLLC/BEN2", filename="BEN2_Base.pth", local_dir="tryon/api/ben2")# Then use custom pathadapter = BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter( weights_path="tryon/api/ben2/BEN2_Base.pth") Image Format Issues​ BEN2 automatically converts images to RGB: # RGBA images are converted to RGB automaticallyresult = adapter.remove_background("image_with_alpha.png")# Grayscale images are also convertedresult = adapter.remove_background("grayscale.jpg") API Reference Summary​ Method Description remove_background(image, refine=False) Remove background from single image remove_background_batch(images, refine=False) Remove background from multiple images load_image(input_data) Load image from path, URL, or BytesIO Related Documentation​ Preprocessing Overview Garment Segmentation Virtual Try-On API Kling AI References​ BEN2 on Hugging Face Swin Transformer Paper Edit this page Previous Clad body measurements (API) Next Kimi K2.6 / K2.7 Code / K3 / K3.1 Pro Understanding Overview Key Features Requirements Installation Quick Start Single Image Batch Processing Command Line Usage CLI Arguments Python API BEN2BackgroundRemoverAdapter Use Cases Virtual Try-On Preprocessing E-Commerce Product Photos Model Swap Preprocessing Performance Tips GPU Acceleration Batch Processing Refinement Trade-offs Model Architecture Troubleshooting Common Issues API Reference Summary Related Documentation References

API Reference Claude Haiku 5.5 Understanding On this page Claude Haiku 5.5 Understanding Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5, released 7 Oct 2026) is Anthropic's fastest and cheapest tier, built for high-volume, latency-sensitive work such as classification, extraction and routing. OpenTryOn exposes it through the understand service with ClaudeUnderstandAdapter (first-party Messages API, anthropic SDK). Good fits in fashion pipelines: tagging garment attributes, reading care labels and size tags, writing alt-text and product copy, and cheap QC passes over generated try-on images. Property Value Model id claude-haiku-5-5 Input / output Text and images in, text out (no video) Context / max output 1M tokens / 128K tokens Price From $0.10 / $0.50 per MTok (input / output), 50% off on Batch Thinking Adaptive, on by default; effort low / medium (default) / high / xhigh / max Authentication​ export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." This is the same key the Studio chat planner already uses when OPENTRYON_AGENT_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic. CLI​ opentryon understand --model claude-haiku-5-5 \ --image garment.jpg --prompt "List fabric, colour, fit and neckline as JSON."# Cheapest/fastest: low effort, thinking off (thinking can only be disabled at high effort or below)opentryon understand --model claude-haiku-5-5 --image label.jpg \ --prompt "Transcribe the care label." --effort low --no-thinking# Text-only also worksopentryon understand --model claude-haiku-5-5 --prompt "Write a 20-word product blurb for a linen shirt." Flag Notes --image, -i Optional image (path or URL; URLs are passed through, files are base64-encoded) --prompt, -p Question or instruction --system Optional system prompt --effort low, medium, high, xhigh, max (API default medium) --no-thinking Sends thinking: {"type": "disabled"}; rejected at xhigh / max --max-tokens Output cap, including thinking (default 4096) temperature, top_p and top_k are deliberately not exposed: Haiku 5.5 returns HTTP 400 for any non-default value. Python​ from tryon.api.claude import ClaudeUnderstandAdapteradapter = ClaudeUnderstandAdapter() # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEYresult = adapter.understand( image="garment.jpg", prompt="Describe the outfit in one sentence.", effort="low", thinking=False,)print(result["text"], result["usage"]) understand_image(image, ...) accepts a list of images for multi-image comparison. Notes​ MCP tool: understand_claude_haiku_5_5 (generated from the registry). Planner: claude haiku 5.5 / haiku 5.5 / claude-haiku-5-5 pin this model. The understand default stays kimi-k2.6. Haiku 5.5 uses the newer tokenizer (about 30% more tokens than Haiku 4.5 for the same text) — budget --max-tokens accordingly. Cloud-only: Anthropic publishes no open weights. See also: Kimi, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek, GLM. Edit this page Previous DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Understanding Next Typesafe AI Jev (Decisions) Authentication CLI Python Notes

API Reference Cosmos 3 Nano variants Cosmos 3 Nano variants These three ids talk to a self-hosted Cosmos 3 certified NIM. They are not the hosted build.nvidia.com video API. Already shipped, and unchanged: CLI id What it is cosmos3 Hosted Generator nano, text-to-video and image-to-video cosmos3-reasoner Hosted Reasoner nano cosmos3-local Diffusers weights nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano New, certified NIM only (COSMOS3_NIM_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1/infer): CLI id Service NIM_MODEL_VARIANT model_mode cosmos3-nano-t2i generate nano text2image cosmos3-nano-v2v video-generate nano video2video cosmos3-nano-droid robot-act nano-droid policy The hosted catalog endpoint does not serve stills, video-to-video, or the DROID policy. Start the container yourself and point COSMOS3_NIM_URL at it. Port 8010 is the default so it does not collide with TryOn Studio's MCP server on 8000. opentryon generate --model cosmos3-nano-t2i --prompt "linen shirt, soft studio light"opentryon video-generate --model cosmos3-nano-v2v --video clip.mp4 --prompt "slower turn"opentryon robot-act --model cosmos3-nano-droid --image obs.jpg --prompt "pick up the cup" --observation obs.json obs.json needs observation/joint_position (seven numbers) and observation/gripper_position. Nano-DROID returns an action chunk and no video. A bearer token is sent only when NVIDIA_API_KEY or NGC_API_KEY is set. Super checkpoints (super-t2i, super-i2v, and the 4-step students) are not registered. Edit this page Previous NVIDIA NIM (Nemotron / Cosmos) Next Moondream

API Reference Open Decision Models (Decider, Clef, Kev, JEV) On this page Open Decision Models: Decider, Clef, Kev, JEV "System One" decision models don't write text. You send a state (text, JSON, sometimes images) and named, typed questions, and get calibrated answers back in one forward pass. They all use the same question schema as Typesafe Jev: { "formal": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this formal wear?"}, "category": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Garment category?", "criteria": {"dress": "one-piece gowns", "top": "shirts and blouses"}}, "fit": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How fitted is it?", "criteria": ["loose", "regular", "slim"]}} Answers come back as {"model", "answers", "usage"}: noul gives P(yes), choice gives the pick plus probabilities and confidence, and score gives a probability-weighted level with a legend. At a glance​ Registry id Model Hosting Images Needs pplx-decider Perplexity Decider v1.2 (27B) / Flash v1.2 (4B) Perplexity Decisions API (first-party) up to 8 PERPLEXITY_API_KEY pplx-decider-local perplexity-ai/pplx-decider-v1.1-27b your SGLang server up to 8 80 GB-class GPU clef Cloudflare Clef (27B) / Clef-flash (9B) Workers AI (first-party) up to 4 CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID clef-local Cloudflare/clef your SGLang server up to 4 80 GB+ GPU (tested on H200) kev-openrouter Kev 4B OpenRouter (third-party; Kev has no first-party API) no OPENROUTER_API_KEY kev-local Kev 0.8B / 4B / 9B / 27B the Kev repo's kev.serve no 4 GB GPU (0.8B) to 80 GB (27B); MLX on Apple Silicon autotrust-jev-local AutoTrust JEV-35B / JEV-35B-NVFP4 / JEV-27B-VL your vLLM serve.sh (no hosted API exists) up to 8 32 GB (NVFP4) to 80 GB GPU All four model families publish Apache-2.0 weights. Vendor benchmarks are self-reported. Perplexity Decider​ Decider replaces Qwen3.8-27B's language head with a 255-way answer-code readout, with non-causal attention in its full-attention layers. export PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=...opentryon decide --model pplx-decider --questions questions.json --state "Red satin evening gown, floor length"opentryon decide --model pplx-decider --decider-model pplx-decider-flash-v1.2 --questions questions.json --image dress.jpgopentryon decide --model pplx-decider --questions questions.json --state "Is this brand in stock at Nordstrom?" --web-grounding Endpoint: POST https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/decisions. Up to 255 options per choice, 10 levels per score. Images go inside state as data-URL parts (PNG, JPEG, WebP). Remote image URLs are downloaded and inlined, because the API rejects them. --web-grounding lets Decider search the web first; searches are billed separately. --max-staleness sets the oldest cached result it may use, in seconds. Self-hosted: serve the open weights with a nightly SGLang build, then point OpenTryOn at it. export PPLX_DECIDER_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 # defaultopentryon decide --model pplx-decider-local --questions questions.json --state "..." --image dress.jpg Cloudflare Clef​ Clef adds a joint schema head on a frozen Qwen backbone. The head routes evidence between the state, the questions and their options and scores the whole schema together. export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=... # a Workers AI API tokenexport CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=...opentryon decide --model clef --questions questions.json --state "..." --image look.jpgopentryon decide --model clef --clef-model clef-flash --questions questions.json --state "..." clef clef-flash Size 27B (Qwen3.8-27B) 9B (Qwen3.5-9B) Context 65,536 tokens 24,576 tokens Input price $0.24 per M tokens $0.038 per M tokens Up to 64 questions and 4 images (PNG, JPEG, WebP; 4 MiB each) per request. Output tokens are free and Cloudflare lists zero data retention. Prices are Cloudflare's published rates at the time of writing. Self-hosted: run Cloudflare's SGLang image (lmsysorg/sglang:dev-clef, sglang serve --model-path Cloudflare/clef --port 30000), then use --model clef-local (CLEF_BASE_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:30000). Kev (Jared Palmer)​ Kev is a LoRA plus a small pointer head on Qwen base models. The pointer head scores each option against the question while the state's computation is shared across questions. Kev has no first-party API. # Hosted, through OpenRouter's System One endpoint (Kev 4B, 8K context)export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...opentryon decide --model kev-openrouter --questions questions.json --state "Customer was charged twice for order 1182"# Self-hosted, any size, with the Kev repo's servergit clone https://github.com/jaredpalmer/kev.git && cd kev && uv sync --extra serveuv run --extra serve python -m kev.serve --run jaredpalmer/kev-4b --port 8008opentryon decide --model kev-local --questions questions.json --state "..." Kev is text-only: pass image descriptions or product data as the state. KEV_API_KEY is only needed if you set one on your server. AutoTrust JEV​ AutoTrust's JEV builds open System One models around a learned decision block (a LoRA plus decision head) on a frozen Qwen backbone, and it reads images. It is a separate company and model from Typesafe's Jev (--model jev). AutoTrust runs no hosted API and no third-party host serves JEV, so autotrust-jev-local talks to the server you start yourself: hf download autotrust/JEV-35B --local-dir JEV-35B # or autotrust/JEV-35B-NVFP4 for a 32 GB GPUbash JEV-35B/serve.sh # vLLM + POST /v1/decide on :8000opentryon decide --model autotrust-jev-local --questions questions.json --state "..." --image look.jpg JEV's /v1/decide answers one question per request, so OpenTryOn sends one request per question and maps the replies onto the shared answer shape: noul: the server scores false and true; the answer is P(true). choice: criteria keys become the options, and their descriptions are added to the question. score: JEV's native score is a fixed 0–5 scale, so your ordered levels are asked as a choice over the levels, and score is the probability-weighted level index. Python​ from tryon.api.perplexity import PerplexityDeciderAdapterfrom tryon.api.cloudflare import ClefAdapterfrom tryon.api.systemone import SystemOneAdapterfrom tryon.api.autotrust import AutoTrustJevAdapterquestions = {"formal": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this formal wear?"}}PerplexityDeciderAdapter().decide(questions, state="Red satin gown", image=["gown.jpg"])ClefAdapter(model="clef-flash").decide(questions, state="Red satin gown")SystemOneAdapter(preset="kev-local").decide(questions, state="Red satin gown")AutoTrustJevAdapter().decide(questions, state="Red satin gown") SystemOneAdapter works with any server that speaks the /v1/systemone contract. Presets: kev-openrouter, kev-local, clef-local and pplx-decider-local. Already integrated​ Three other decision models from the same wave were already in the decide service: Typesafe Jev (jev), Liquid AI d1 (d1-3b, d1-omni-600m) and the vLLM Semantic Router D3 family (d3-turbo to d3-edge, hosted and local). Sources​ Perplexity Decisions API · pplx-decider-v1.1-27b Workers AI: Clef · Cloudflare/clef jaredpalmer/kev-4b · OpenRouter System One autotrust/JEV-35B · autotrust/JEV-27B-VL Edit this page Previous Typesafe AI Jev (Decisions) Next vLLM-SR Decision 3.0 (hosted) At a glance Perplexity Decider Cloudflare Clef Kev (Jared Palmer) AutoTrust JEV Python Already integrated Sources

API Reference DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Understanding On this page DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Understanding deepseek-flash is DeepSeek's multimodal Flash model (general availability since 10 Sep 2026, formerly previewed as V4-Flash-Vision-Exp) via the DeepSeek Platform's OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API. OpenTryOn integrates it via DeepSeekUnderstandAdapter for image understanding — currently the cheapest frontier-class VLM available. Like Kimi, Qwen3.8, and GLM-5.3-FlashX, it is general-purpose — useful for describing garments and outfits in the fashion domain, but equally capable on documents, UI screenshots, product photography, or any other image content. For open-weight DeepSeek models that run on your own GPU instead of this hosted API — DeepSeek has no first-party hosted endpoint for them — see DeepSeek-VL2 (general multimodal understanding) and DeepSeek-OCR (document/label OCR). Unlike those three, DeepSeek's API does not accept video input — images only. Capabilities​ Capability deepseek-flash Notes Modalities Text, image in Text out. No video. Context 1M tokens 384K max output Thinking On by default reasoning_effort: none disables it Reasoning depth reasoning_effort: none, low, high (default), max Trades thoroughness vs latency/cost Architecture Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED), MoE 8B active on input / 16B on output from a 552B backbone Pricing ~$0.15 input / $0.60 output per 1M tokens (off-peak) Images billed up to 384 tokens each Legacy model names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted upstream but are served and billed as deepseek-flash — this adapter only exposes the canonical id. Prerequisites​ DeepSeek Platform account and API key: platform.deepseek.com Set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in your .env file Optional base URL override via DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=your_deepseek_api_key# DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com # default Installation​ The DeepSeek adapter reuses the openai package (already a core dependency of opentryon, since the DeepSeek API is OpenAI-SDK compatible). No additional installation is required. Quick Start​ from tryon.api.deepseek import DeepSeekUnderstandAdapteradapter = DeepSeekUnderstandAdapter() # deepseek-flash by defaultresult = adapter.understand_image( "garment.jpg", prompt="Describe this outfit: color, pattern, style, fit, and material.",)print(result["text"])print(result["reasoning"]) # thinking content when enabled Public https:// image URLs are passed through; local files are inlined as base64 data URIs. CLI​ opentryon understand --model deepseek-flash \ --image garment.jpg --prompt "Describe this outfit."opentryon understand --model deepseek-flash \ --image garment.jpg --reasoning-effort none # disable thinkingopentryon understand --model deepseek-flash \ --image garment.jpg --reasoning-effort max --prompt "What's the fabric?" --image is required — there is no text-only or video path for this model. MCP​ Same registry model appears as an MCP tool (no extra wiring): understand_deepseek_flash — DeepSeek Platform API (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY) See MCP Server and mcp-server/README.md. API Reference​ DeepSeekUnderstandAdapter​ class DeepSeekUnderstandAdapter: def __init__( self, api_key: Optional[str] = None, # DEEPSEEK_API_KEY model: str = "deepseek-flash", base_url: Optional[str] = None, # DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL or the default ) Methods​ understand_image(image, prompt, reasoning_effort=None, max_tokens=None) understand(image=..., prompt=..., ...) — CLI / MCP entry point; raises ValueError if image is omitted Return dict keys: text, reasoning, model, usage. References​ DeepSeek API pricing & models DeepSeek Chat Completions API V4-Flash-Vision-Exp release notes Edit this page Previous GLM-5.3-FlashX Understanding Next Claude Haiku 5.5 Understanding Capabilities Prerequisites Installation Quick Start CLI MCP API Reference DeepSeekUnderstandAdapter Methods References

API Reference Dream Labs Dream-1 On this page Dream Labs Dream-1 Dream-1 is Dream Labs' World Action Model (WAM): a hosted policy that maps camera frames + robot state to short action chunks (~1.6 seconds). It targets bimanual parallel-gripper arms and is meant for zero-shot control of unseen embodiments (research beta — not safety-validated). OpenTryOn exposes it on the robot-act service (API only). There is no local Dream-1 policy checkpoint to run on your GPU; inference is through Dream Labs' gateway (POST /v1/get_action). Registry id Checkpoint Notes dream-1 dreamlabs/dream-1 Full model (~$3/hr on Dream Labs pricing) dream-1-flash dreamlabs/dream-1-flash Faster tier (~$2/hr) Video world models (DreamDojo / GR-1) use a separate dream-engine SDK — not wired here. Prerequisites​ pip install dreamlabs-client # import dreamexport DREAM_API_KEY=dl_live_... # platform / Dream Labs setup Optional credentials file (~/.dreamlabs/credentials): DREAM_GATEWAY_URL=https://api.dreamlabs.aiDREAM_API_URL=https://platform.dreamlabs.aiDREAM_DATA_URL=https://data.dreamlabs.aiDREAM_API_KEY=dl_live_... One policy step (CLI)​ Each CLI call performs policy → set_observation → get_action → close (one action chunk). Production loops call set_observation every camera tick and get_action on a worker thread — see the dreamlabs-client README. opentryon robot-act --model dream-1 \ --frames frames.json \ --observation obs.json \ --policy-config yam_policy.jsonopentryon robot-act --model dream-1-flash --frames frames.json --observation obs.json --dry-run frames.json (example)​ { "video.overhead": "<base64 JPEG, no data: prefix>", "video.wrist_l": "<base64 JPEG>", "video.wrist_r": "<base64 JPEG>"} obs.json (example)​ { "state.right_arm": [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], "state.right_gripper": [0.5], "state.left_arm": [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], "state.left_gripper": [0.5], "prompt": "fold the towel"} Use float arrays compatible with your embodiment; YAM examples and ik / embodiment blocks are in the official client docs. Python​ from tryon.api.dream_labs import Dream1Adapteradapter = Dream1Adapter(checkpoint="dreamlabs/dream-1")out = adapter.get_action( frames="frames.json", observation="obs.json", policy_config={"strict": True, "ik": {"arm": "yam", "head": "joint"}},)print(out["action"]) MCP​ Tools: robot_act_dream_1, robot_act_dream_1_flash (generated from the registry). Key: DREAM_API_KEY. Local weights​ Not available for Dream-1 policy inference. Dream Labs serves the model; you integrate via dreamlabs-client. For open-weight decision models (fashion QA / routing), see vLLM-SR d3 or Liquid d1. API Reference ElevenLabs Eleven v4 / v4 Turbo (Text-to-Speech) On this page ElevenLabs Eleven v4 / v4 Turbo (Text-to-Speech) Eleven v4 and Eleven v4 Turbo are ElevenLabs' text-to-speech models, called via their first-party REST API. This is OpenTryOn's first tts service -- previously there was no speech modality in the registry at all. Useful on its own (voiceover/narration for lookbook or product copy), or as an input to Pruna P-Video-Avatar (which accepts a pre-generated --audio file) for a talking-head clip with a specific branded/cloned voice. A second TTS vendor is available: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS (gemini-3.8-flash-tts, gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts, GEMINI_API_KEY) with 30 prebuilt voices and two-speaker dialogue. Capabilities​ Capability eleven-v4 eleven-v4-turbo Character limit 10,000 (~10 min of audio) Not explicitly capped Latency Not optimized for real-time ~100ms median inference Languages 90+ 90+ Style Most emotionally rich / expressive Adds audio tags for delivery control, e.g. [whispers], [laughs] Voice cloning Yes (via voice_id) Yes (via voice_id) Output formats mp3, wav, pcm, opus, µ-law, A-law at various sample rates/bitrates Same Both models are billed per character; see elevenlabs.io/pricing/api for current rates. Prerequisites​ ElevenLabs account and API key: elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys Set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY in your .env file Optional base URL override via ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=your_elevenlabs_api_key# ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL=https://api.elevenlabs.io # default Voices​ The adapter defaults voice_id to ElevenLabs' premade "Rachel" voice (21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM) so you can try it without first looking one up. Browse or clone voices at elevenlabs.io/app/voice-library, or list your account's voices with GET /v1/voices (not wrapped by this adapter -- use ElevenLabs' own SDK/dashboard for voice management; this adapter is generation-only). Installation​ No extra install -- the adapter only uses requests, already a core opentryon dependency. Quick Start​ from tryon.api.elevenlabs import ElevenLabsAdapteradapter = ElevenLabsAdapter() # eleven_v4 by defaultaudio = adapter.generate_speech( "Welcome to the spring collection.", voice_id="21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM", # optional; this is the default)open("voiceover.mp3", "wb").write(audio) Eleven v4 Turbo with audio tags​ turbo = ElevenLabsAdapter(model="eleven_v4_turbo")audio = turbo.generate_speech("[whispers] New drop just landed.")open("teaser.mp3", "wb").write(audio) CLI​ opentryon tts --model eleven-v4 --text "Welcome to the spring collection."opentryon tts --model eleven-v4-turbo \ --text "[whispers] New drop just landed." \ --voice-id 21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM --output-format wav_44100opentryon tts --model eleven-v4 --text "Bonjour et bienvenue." --language-code fr opentryon writes the result with an extension sniffed from the actual audio bytes (.mp3/.wav/.opus; headerless formats like raw PCM or µ-law fall back to .raw), not from the requested --output-format string, so it's always correct even if a request is retried with a different format. Flag Notes --text / -t Required. Eleven v4: up to 10,000 characters --voice-id Default: premade "Rachel" (21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM) --output-format Codec/sample-rate/bitrate; default mp3_44100_128 --language-code Optional ISO 639-1 code to force text normalization --stability / --similarity-boost / --style / --speed Voice settings (0-1 range, except --speed) --no-speaker-boost Disable enhanced speaker similarity --seed Optional deterministic-sampling seed MCP​ Same registry models appear as MCP tools (no extra wiring): tts_eleven_v4 / tts_eleven_v4_turbo — ElevenLabs API (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY) See MCP Server and mcp-server/README.md. Studio note: tts is a brand-new service category, so it does not yet have a dedicated capability picker screen in TryOn Studio (those are currently Image / VTON / Understand / Video / BG Remove). The MCP tools are live and callable (e.g. via Studio's Agent chat) as soon as the MCP server restarts; a dedicated Studio screen would be a separate tryon-studio-side change. API Reference​ ElevenLabsAdapter​ class ElevenLabsAdapter: def __init__( self, api_key: Optional[str] = None, # ELEVENLABS_API_KEY model: str = "eleven_v4", # or "eleven_v4_turbo" base_url: Optional[str] = None, # ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL or the default ) generate_speech​ def generate_speech( self, text: str, voice_id: str = "21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM", model: Optional[str] = None, output_format: str = "mp3_44100_128", language_code: Optional[str] = None, stability: float = 0.5, similarity_boost: float = 0.75, style: float = 0.0, speed: float = 1.0, use_speaker_boost: bool = True, seed: Optional[int] = None,) -> bytes Returns raw audio bytes (content type matches output_format). This is what opentryon tts --model eleven-v4 calls. API Reference MiniMax H3 Max (Fal) On this page MiniMax H3 Max (Fal) OpenTryOn’s first third-party hoster adapter. Fal jointly released MiniMax H3 Max with MiniMax and hosts a post-trained stack with T2V, I2V, reference-to-video, a dedicated lip-sync/dubbing endpoint, and video relighting. This is not the MiniMax first-party V2 API. Official MiniMax H3 Max (--model minimax-h3-max, MINIMAX_API_KEY) is T2V / first-last I2V only. Use Fal when you want R2V, lip-sync, or Fal’s queue. CLI model Host Modes Key minimax-h3-max MiniMax V2 T2V, I2V MINIMAX_API_KEY fal-h3-max Fal queue T2V, I2V, R2V FAL_KEY fal-h3-max-lipsync Fal queue Image + audio → lip-synced video FAL_KEY fal-h3-max-relight Fal queue Video + lighting-sphere image → relit video FAL_KEY minimax-h3 MiniMax V2 T2V, I2V, R2V (Python), 2K MINIMAX_API_KEY No open weights for H3 Max. Local H3-Base is --model minimax-h3-local. Docs: T2V, I2V, R2V, Lip Sync, Relight, queue. Environment​ export FAL_KEY=... # https://fal.ai/dashboard/keys# export FAL_API_KEY=... # alias# export FAL_QUEUE_BASE_URL=https://queue.fal.run Auth header is Authorization: Key {FAL_KEY} (not Bearer). CLI​ opentryon video-generate --model fal-h3-max \ --prompt "A fashion model walking a runway at dusk, camera tracking" \ --duration 5 --resolution 768P --ratio 16:9opentryon video-generate --model fal-h3-max \ --image look.jpg --prompt "Gentle fabric motion as the model turns" \ --duration 6opentryon video-generate --model fal-h3-max \ --prompt "Walk toward camera, stop on the mark" \ --last-frame end.jpgopentryon video-generate --model fal-h3-max \ --prompt "Image 1 is the model. Keep her identity while she walks the runway." \ --reference-image look.jpg \ --duration 5 --resolution 768P# Lip-sync / dubbing: portrait + audio in, matched mouth movement out (no prompt)opentryon video-generate --model fal-h3-max-lipsync \ --image portrait.jpg --audio line.wav \ --resolution 1080P --enable-transcription# Relight an existing clip from a lighting-sphere render (no prompt)opentryon video-generate --model fal-h3-max-relight \ --video runway.mp4 --reference-image warm_sunset_sphere.png --resolution 1080P Flag Notes --duration Integer 5–15 seconds (default 5) --resolution 480P or 768P (default 768P) --ratio T2V: 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 (not adaptive). R2V may use adaptive. I2V follows the keyframe. --image First frame (switches to I2V) --last-frame Last frame (alone or with --image) --reference-image / --reference-video / --reference-audio R2V lists. At most 12 files total. Audio cannot be the only reference. Mutually exclusive with --image. --prompt-expansion balanced (default) or quality --no-safety-checker Disable Fal’s safety checker --seed Optional fal-h3-max-lipsync flags​ No --prompt — only an image and an audio track. Resolution ceiling is higher than T2V/I2V/R2V (up to 2K). Flag Notes --image Portrait to animate (aspect ratio must be 0.4–2.5) — required --audio Track to sync mouth movement to (≥5s; clipped to ~14.8s) — required --resolution 480P, 768P, 1080P, or 2K (default 768P) --enable-transcription Transcribe the audio to guide lip-sync accuracy --no-safety-checker Disable Fal’s safety checker --seed Optional fal-h3-max-relight flags​ Video-to-video: subjects, motion, camera and audio are preserved; only the lighting changes to match a lighting-sphere render. There is no prompt field — the sphere image fully defines the lighting. Flag Notes --video Source clip (path or URL), up to 15 s; converted to 24 fps and trimmed to a valid frame count (≥ ~2.33 s) — required --reference-image Lighting-sphere render that defines the target lighting — required --resolution 480P, 768P, 1080P, or 2K (default 768P; 1080P / 2K are upscaled and refined from 768P) --aspect-ratio adaptive, 21:9, 16:9 (default), 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 --no-safety-checker Disable Fal’s safety checker --seed Optional Fal pricing is per output second: $0.05 (480p), $0.08 (768p), $0.16 (1080p), $0.32 (2K). Python​ from tryon.api.fal import FalH3MaxAdapteradapter = FalH3MaxAdapter()open("t2v.mp4", "wb").write( adapter.generate_text_to_video( prompt="A fashion model walking a runway at dusk", duration=5, resolution="768P", ratio="16:9", ))open("i2v.mp4", "wb").write( adapter.generate_image_to_video( image="look.jpg", prompt="Gentle turn toward the camera", last_frame="end.jpg", ))open("r2v.mp4", "wb").write( adapter.generate_text_to_video( prompt="Image 1 is the model. Keep her identity while she walks.", reference_image=["look.jpg"], ))open("lipsync.mp4", "wb").write( adapter.generate_lip_sync( image="portrait.jpg", audio="line.wav", resolution="1080P", ))open("relit.mp4", "wb").write( adapter.generate_relight( video="runway.mp4", reference_image="warm_sunset_sphere.png", resolution="1080P", )) Notes​ Jobs go through Fal’s queue (POST https://queue.fal.run/minimax/h3-max/... → poll status_url → download video.url). MCP tools: video_generate_fal_h3_max, video_generate_fal_h3_max_lipsync and video_generate_fal_h3_max_relight (generated from the registry). Planner: fal h3 max / fal-h3-max pin T2V/I2V/R2V. h3 max lip sync / fal-h3-max-lipsync pin the dubbing endpoint. h3 max relight / fal-h3-max-relight pin the relight endpoint. A bare h3 max still pins first-party minimax-h3-max. API Reference FASHN AI Virtual Try-On On this page FASHN AI Virtual Try-On The FashnVTONAdapter provides an interface to FASHN's fashion-focused virtual try-on endpoints. Overview​ FASHN exposes a universal POST /v1/run + GET /v1/status/{id} API. This adapter covers the two primary try-on models: Model Registry id Best for tryon-max fashn-tryon-max High-fidelity photoshoots / e-commerce catalogs (up to 4K, prompt-based styling) tryon-v1.6 fashn-tryon-v1.6 Fast real-time try-on (1 credit/image, ~5–8s) Open-weight twin: FASHN open-sourced VTON v1.5 (Apache-2.0). Run it on your own GPU with --model fashn-vton-1.5 — see FASHN VTON v1.5 (local). Location note: like Pruna's P-Image-Try-On, this adapter lives under tryon.api.vton (a use-case directory) rather than a dedicated tryon.api.fashn/ package -- see Adding a New Model Integration. References: FASHN docs Try-On Max Try-On v1.6 Python SDK (optional; this adapter uses requests directly) Authentication​ export FASHN_API_KEY="your_api_key" Or pass api_key= to the constructor. Keys are created in the FASHN Developer API dashboard. Quick Start​ from dotenv import load_dotenvload_dotenv()from tryon.api.vton import FashnVTONAdapteradapter = FashnVTONAdapter()# Try-On Max (recommended)images = adapter.generate_and_decode( model_image="data/model-1.jpg", product_image="data/garment.png", model_name="tryon-max", resolution="2k", generation_mode="quality",)images[0].save("outputs/fashn_max.png")# Try-On v1.6 (fast)images = adapter.generate_and_decode( model_image="data/model-1.jpg", product_image="data/garment.png", model_name="tryon-v1.6", mode="performance",)images[0].save("outputs/fashn_v16.png") API Reference​ Class: FashnVTONAdapter​ Constructor​ FashnVTONAdapter(api_key: Optional[str] = None, base_url: Optional[str] = None) Methods​ generate(...) / generate_and_decode(...)​ Common person/garment aliases: model_image / person / source_image and product_image / garment / garment_image. The adapter maps the garment field to product_image (tryon-max) or garment_image (tryon-v1.6) automatically. Shared options: seed, output_format (png|jpeg), return_base64, max_wait_time. tryon-max options: prompt, resolution (1k|2k|4k), generation_mode (fast|balanced|quality), num_images (1–4). tryon-v1.6 options: category, mode, garment_photo_type, moderation_level, segmentation_free, num_samples (1–4). generate() returns a list of CDN URLs (or data URIs when return_base64=True). generate_and_decode() returns List[PIL.Image.Image]. After a successful call, adapter.last_prediction_id and adapter.last_credits_used are set from the response. Catalogue endpoints (product-to-model, model swap, …)​ Beyond try-on, FASHN exposes the e-commerce photo workflow. tryon.api.fashn.FashnAdapter (it extends FashnVTONAdapter, so it uses the same FASHN_API_KEY, /v1/run + /v1/status protocol and image handling) wraps them: CLI model Service FASHN endpoint What it does Lifecycle fashn-product-to-model edit product-to-model Product photo → a person wearing it. Optional --image-prompt (pose/lighting), --background-reference, --face-reference Preview fashn-model-create generate model-create Prompt (+ optional reference) → a new fashion model photo Experimental fashn-model-swap edit model-swap Change the model's face / skin / hair, keep outfit and pose Experimental fashn-face-to-model edit face-to-model Headshot → try-on-ready upper-body avatar (vertical ratios only) Experimental fashn-reframe edit reframe Expand or crop to a target aspect ratio Experimental fashn-edit edit edit Prompt edit with optional --mask and --image-context — fashn-image-to-video video-generate image-to-video Animate a still, 5 or 10 s, 480p–1080p, optional --end-image — fashn-bg-remove bg-remove background-remove Transparent-background cut-out, 1 credit — Product-to-model is not try-on. It generates a new person wearing the product and does not keep an existing photo's pose or background; use fashn-tryon-max with a person photo for that. The usual chain for a catalogue with no studio shots is fashn-face-to-model → fashn-tryon-max, or fashn-product-to-model directly. Credits (as published by FASHN): the image endpoints cost generation_mode × resolution (fast / balanced / quality × 1k / 2k / 4k = 1–5 credits), --face-reference adds +3 per image, and --num-images multiplies the total. Video is 1 / 3 / 6 credits for 5 s and 2 / 6 / 12 for 10 s at 480p / 720p / 1080p. Background remove is 1. If --generation-mode is omitted FASHN picks one and bills accordingly. opentryon edit --model fashn-product-to-model \ --image jacket.jpg --prompt "tucked-in, studio background" \ --aspect-ratio 4:5 --resolution 2k --generation-mode balancedopentryon edit --model fashn-model-swap --model-image look.jpg \ --face-reference campaign_face.jpg --face-reference-mode match_baseopentryon generate --model fashn-model-create \ --prompt "Full body shot, woman in a white t-shirt and dark blue biker shorts"opentryon edit --model fashn-reframe --image look.jpg --aspect-ratio 9:16opentryon video-generate --model fashn-image-to-video --image look.jpg --duration 5 --resolution 720popentryon bg-remove --model fashn-bg-remove --image product.jpg from tryon.api.fashn import FashnAdapteradapter = FashnAdapter()images = adapter.generate_product_to_model("jacket.jpg", prompt="studio background", resolution="2k")video = adapter.generate_image_to_video("look.jpg", duration=5, resolution="720p") # MP4 bytes Image endpoints return decoded PIL images (the adapter requests base64 output, so results do not depend on CDN expiry). The adapter validates resolution tier, quality mode, num_images (1–4), per-endpoint aspect ratios, and that --face-reference-mode is only used with --face-reference. Pricing and parameters come from FASHN's docs (checked 13 Oct 2026); these endpoints were integrated without live calls, so confirm credit costs on your account. MCP tools: edit_fashn_product_to_model, generate_fashn_model_create, edit_fashn_model_swap, edit_fashn_face_to_model, edit_fashn_reframe, edit_fashn_edit, video_generate_fashn_image_to_video, bg_remove_fashn_bg_remove. Planner pins: fashn product to model, fashn model swap, fashn model create, fashn face to model, fashn reframe, fashn edit, fashn image to video. opentryon CLI / MCP Server​ opentryon vton --model fashn-tryon-max \ --model-image model.png --garment-image garment.png \ --resolution 2k --generation-mode qualityopentryon vton --model fashn-tryon-v1.6 \ --model-image model.png --garment-image garment.png --mode performance MCP tools: vton_fashn_tryon_max, vton_fashn_tryon_v1_6. API Reference FLUX 3 Image On this page FLUX 3 Image FLUX 3 Image is Black Forest Labs' unified still-image endpoint: one model handles text-to-image, edits, and compositions from up to 10 reference images. OpenTryOn exposes it as flux3-image on the generate and edit services (same adapter class, same BFL_API_KEY). For the faster distilled sibling, see FLUX 3 Image Klein (flux3-image-klein). For video, see FLUX 3 Video (flux3-video). Prerequisites​ BFL_API_KEY=your_bfl_api_key Sign up and create a key in the BFL dashboard. CLI​ # Text-to-imageopentryon generate --model flux3-image \ --prompt "Editorial fashion still, soft window light" \ --aspect-ratio 3:4 --resolution 2k# Edit with one referenceopentryon edit --model flux3-image \ --image data/model-1.jpg \ --prompt "Change the blazer to deep burgundy velvet"# Dry-run (no API call)opentryon generate --model flux3-image --prompt "test" --dry-run Notable flags​ Flag Default Notes --aspect-ratio auto Many ratios plus auto (follows first reference or prompt) --resolution 1k 768sq, 1k, 1.5k, 2k, 4k --safety-tolerance 2 0 (strictest) through 4 --no-grounding grounding on Skip web/image search pre-step for faster runs --reference-images — Edit only — extra refs beyond --image (10 total) Layout control uses bounding boxes in the prompt (JSON on a 0–1000 grid); see the BFL bounding-box tutorial. Python​ from tryon.api import Flux3ImageAdapteradapter = Flux3ImageAdapter()images = adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="Minimal product photo on warm stone", aspect_ratio="16:9", resolution="1k",)images[0].save("outputs/flux3_t2i.png")edited = adapter.generate_image_edit( prompt="Replace the background with a runway set", input_image="data/model-1.jpg", resolution="2k",)edited[0].save("outputs/flux3_edit.png") MCP​ After registry changes, restart the MCP server. Tools are generated from the registry: generate_flux3_image edit_flux3_image Both unlock when BFL_API_KEY is set in the OpenTryOn .env (Studio Connect passthrough). API details​ Submit: POST https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-3-image with x-key Poll: use the returned polling_url until status is Ready Download: result.sample (signed URL; download within about one hour) Rejected fields: FLUX.2-only fields such as width, height, and seed return HTTP 422 on this endpoint Related​ FLUX.2 Image Generation — separate PRO/FLEX endpoints with pixel width/height Virtual try-on remains on the dedicated flux-vto model (vton service); see CLI. API Reference FLUX 3 Image Klein On this page FLUX 3 Image Klein FLUX 3 Image Klein is Black Forest Labs' compact, open-weights sibling to FLUX 3 Image. The hosted API uses the same unified contract: text-to-image, edits, multi-reference composition (up to 10 images), and bounding-box layout prompts — without the full model's grounding field. OpenTryOn exposes it as flux3-image-klein on generate and edit (same BFL_API_KEY as FLUX.2 / FLUX 3 Image / FLUX 3 Video). Prerequisites​ BFL_API_KEY=your_bfl_api_key Sign up and create a key in the BFL dashboard. CLI​ # Text-to-image (distilled default ~16 steps on the API)opentryon generate --model flux3-image-klein \ --prompt "Editorial fashion still, soft window light" \ --aspect-ratio 3:4 --resolution 2k# Reproducible outputopentryon generate --model flux3-image-klein \ --prompt "Lookbook flat lay" --seed 42 --steps 12# Edit with one referenceopentryon edit --model flux3-image-klein \ --image data/model-1.jpg \ --prompt "Change the blazer to deep burgundy velvet"# Dry-run (no API call)opentryon generate --model flux3-image-klein --prompt "test" --dry-run Klein vs full FLUX 3 Image​ flux3-image-klein flux3-image Endpoint /v1/flux-3-image-klein /v1/flux-3-image Grounding Not supported Optional (--no-grounding) Safety tolerance 0–7 0–4 Extra knobs --seed, --steps (1–16), --output-format — Exact pixels --width + --height (overrides resolution/ratio) Resolution tiers only Layout control uses the same bounding-box JSON appended to the prompt; see the BFL bounding-box tutorial. Python​ from tryon.api import Flux3ImageKleinAdapteradapter = Flux3ImageKleinAdapter()images = adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="Editorial fashion still", aspect_ratio="3:4", resolution="2k", seed=0, steps=16,)images[0].save("outputs/flux3_klein_t2i.png")edited = adapter.generate_image_edit( prompt="Change jacket to navy wool", input_image="data/model-1.jpg",)edited[0].save("outputs/flux3_klein_edit.png") MCP​ After the OpenTryOn MCP server loads the registry: generate_flux3_image_klein edit_flux3_image_klein Local weights (GPU)​ OpenTryOn registers local inference as flux3-image-klein-local on generate and edit (Flux3ImageKleinLocalAdapter, Diffusers ModularPipeline). See FLUX 3 Image Klein (local) for install, VRAM notes, and CLI examples. Default weights: black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein; base checkpoint via --model-id black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base. API Reference FLUX 3 Max On this page FLUX 3 Max FLUX 3 Max is Black Forest Labs' fastest, highest-quality video tier in the FLUX 3 family. It uses the same async endpoint as FLUX 3 Video (POST https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-3-video) with the harness version field set to max. OpenTryOn exposes it as flux3-max on video-generate (same BFL_API_KEY as flux3-image, flux3-video, and FLUX.2). This is not FLUX 3 Image (still frames) and not FLUX.2 [max] (the previous-generation image model). For general-purpose FLUX 3 video with stylistic range and draft preview, use flux3-video (version=latest by default). Prerequisites​ BFL_API_KEY=your_bfl_api_key# Optional if BFL renames the harness tag:# BFL_FLUX3_MAX_VERSION=max CLI​ Same flags as FLUX 3 Video except there is no --version flag (Max is pinned). opentryon video-generate --model flux3-max \ --prompt "Runway walk, soft key light, camera tracking" \ --aspect-ratio 9:16 --duration 10 --resolution fhdopentryon video-generate --model flux3-max \ --prompt "She turns slowly toward camera" \ --image data/model-1.jpgopentryon video-generate --model flux3-max --prompt "test" --dry-run On flux3-video you can opt into Max explicitly with --version max. API Reference FLUX.2 Image Generation On this page FLUX.2 Image Generation FLUX.2 models provide high-quality image generation capabilities through the BFL AI API. This module includes adapters for both FLUX.2 [PRO] and FLUX.2 [FLEX] models, supporting text-to-image generation, image editing, and multi-image composition. Overview​ FLUX.2 [PRO]: High-quality image generation with standard controls FLUX.2 [FLEX]: Flexible generation with advanced controls (guidance scale, steps, prompt upsampling) Both models support: Text-to-image generation Image editing (prompt + input image) Multi-image composition (up to 8 reference images) Custom width/height control Seed for reproducibility Safety tolerance control Prerequisites​ BFL AI Account: Sign up at BFL AI API Key: Obtain your API key from the BFL AI dashboard Environment Variable: Set BFL_API_KEY in your .env file BFL_API_KEY=your_bfl_api_key Installation​ The FLUX.2 adapters are included in the tryon.api module. No additional installation is required beyond the base dependencies. Quick Start​ FLUX.2 [PRO] - Text-to-Image​ from tryon.api import Flux2ProAdapter# Initialize adapteradapter = Flux2ProAdapter()# Generate image from text promptimages = adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="A professional fashion model wearing elegant evening wear on a runway", width=1024, height=1024, seed=42)# Save resultimages[0].save("outputs/flux2_pro_result.png") FLUX.2 [FLEX] - Advanced Generation​ from tryon.api import Flux2FlexAdapter# Initialize adapteradapter = Flux2FlexAdapter()# Generate with advanced controlsimages = adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="A stylish fashion model wearing elegant evening wear", width=1024, height=1024, guidance=7.5, # Higher guidance = more adherence to prompt steps=50, # More steps = higher quality prompt_upsampling=True, seed=42)images[0].save("outputs/flux2_flex_result.png") API Reference​ Flux2ProAdapter​ __init__(api_key=None, base_url=None)​ Initialize the FLUX.2 [PRO] adapter. Parameters: api_key (str, optional): BFL API key. Defaults to BFL_API_KEY environment variable. base_url (str, optional): Base URL for BFL API. Defaults to https://api.bfl.ai. Raises: ValueError: If API key is not provided. Example: # Using environment variableadapter = Flux2ProAdapter()# Using parameteradapter = Flux2ProAdapter(api_key="your_api_key") generate_text_to_image(prompt, width=None, height=None, seed=None, safety_tolerance=2, output_format="png", **kwargs)​ Generate image from text prompt. Parameters: prompt (str, required): Text description of the image to generate width (int, optional): Width of output image (minimum: 64) height (int, optional): Height of output image (minimum: 64) seed (int, optional): Seed for reproducibility safety_tolerance (int): Moderation tolerance (0-5). 0 = most strict, 5 = least strict. Default: 2 output_format (str): Output format. Options: "jpeg", "png". Default: "png" **kwargs: Additional parameters (webhook_url, webhook_secret, etc.) Returns: List[Image.Image]: List of PIL Image objects Example: images = adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="A professional fashion model wearing elegant evening wear", width=1024, height=1024, seed=42) generate_image_edit(prompt, input_image, width=None, height=None, seed=None, safety_tolerance=2, output_format="png", **kwargs)​ Generate edited image from prompt and input image. Parameters: prompt (str, required): Text description of how to edit the image input_image (Union[str, io.BytesIO, Image.Image], required): Input image (file path, URL, PIL Image, file-like object, or base64) width (int, optional): Width of output image (minimum: 64) height (int, optional): Height of output image (minimum: 64) seed (int, optional): Seed for reproducibility safety_tolerance (int): Moderation tolerance (0-5). Default: 2 output_format (str): Output format. Options: "jpeg", "png". Default: "png" **kwargs: Additional parameters Returns: List[Image.Image]: List of PIL Image objects Example: images = adapter.generate_image_edit( prompt="Change the outfit to casual streetwear style", input_image="model.jpg", width=1024, height=1024) generate_multi_image(prompt, images, width=None, height=None, seed=None, safety_tolerance=2, output_format="png", **kwargs)​ Generate image from multiple input images (composition & style transfer). Parameters: prompt (str, required): Text description of how to combine/transform the images images (List[Union[str, io.BytesIO, Image.Image]], required): List of input images (file paths, URLs, PIL Images, file-like objects, or base64). Maximum 8 images supported. width (int, optional): Width of output image (minimum: 64) height (int, optional): Height of output image (minimum: 64) seed (int, optional): Seed for reproducibility safety_tolerance (int): Moderation tolerance (0-5). Default: 2 output_format (str): Output format. Options: "jpeg", "png". Default: "png" **kwargs: Additional parameters Returns: List[Image.Image]: List of PIL Image objects Raises: ValueError: If more than 8 images are provided. Example: images = adapter.generate_multi_image( prompt="Create a fashion catalog layout combining these clothing styles", images=["outfit1.jpg", "outfit2.jpg", "accessories.jpg"], width=1024, height=1024) Flux2FlexAdapter​ __init__(api_key=None, base_url=None)​ Initialize the FLUX.2 [FLEX] adapter. Parameters: api_key (str, optional): BFL API key. Defaults to BFL_API_KEY environment variable. base_url (str, optional): Base URL for BFL API. Defaults to https://api.bfl.ai. Raises: ValueError: If API key is not provided. generate_text_to_image(prompt, width=None, height=None, seed=None, guidance=3.5, steps=28, prompt_upsampling=True, safety_tolerance=2, output_format="png", **kwargs)​ Generate image from text prompt with advanced controls. Parameters: prompt (str, required): Text description of the image to generate width (int, optional): Width of output image (minimum: 64) height (int, optional): Height of output image (minimum: 64) seed (int, optional): Seed for reproducibility guidance (float): Guidance scale (1.5-10). Higher values = more adherence to prompt. Default: 3.5 steps (int): Number of generation steps. More steps = higher quality. Default: 28 prompt_upsampling (bool): Whether to use prompt upsampling. Default: True safety_tolerance (int): Moderation tolerance (0-5). Default: 2 output_format (str): Output format. Options: "jpeg", "png". Default: "png" **kwargs: Additional parameters (webhook_url, webhook_secret, input_image_blob_path, etc.) Returns: List[Image.Image]: List of PIL Image objects Raises: ValueError: If guidance is not between 1.5 and 10. Example: images = adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="A professional fashion model wearing elegant evening wear", width=1024, height=1024, guidance=7.5, steps=50, prompt_upsampling=True, seed=42) generate_image_edit(prompt, input_image, width=None, height=None, seed=None, guidance=3.5, steps=28, prompt_upsampling=True, safety_tolerance=2, output_format="png", **kwargs)​ Generate edited image from prompt and input image with advanced controls. Parameters: prompt (str, required): Text description of how to edit the image input_image (Union[str, io.BytesIO, Image.Image], required): Input image width (int, optional): Width of output image (minimum: 64) height (int, optional): Height of output image (minimum: 64) seed (int, optional): Seed for reproducibility guidance (float): Guidance scale (1.5-10). Default: 3.5 steps (int): Number of generation steps. Default: 28 prompt_upsampling (bool): Whether to use prompt upsampling. Default: True safety_tolerance (int): Moderation tolerance (0-5). Default: 2 output_format (str): Output format. Options: "jpeg", "png". Default: "png" **kwargs: Additional parameters Returns: List[Image.Image]: List of PIL Image objects generate_multi_image(prompt, images, width=None, height=None, seed=None, guidance=3.5, steps=28, prompt_upsampling=True, safety_tolerance=2, output_format="png", **kwargs)​ Generate image from multiple input images with advanced controls. Parameters: prompt (str, required): Text description of how to combine/transform the images images (List[Union[str, io.BytesIO, Image.Image]], required): List of input images (maximum 8) width (int, optional): Width of output image (minimum: 64) height (int, optional): Height of output image (minimum: 64) seed (int, optional): Seed for reproducibility guidance (float): Guidance scale (1.5-10). Default: 3.5 steps (int): Number of generation steps. Default: 28 prompt_upsampling (bool): Whether to use prompt upsampling. Default: True safety_tolerance (int): Moderation tolerance (0-5). Default: 2 output_format (str): Output format. Options: "jpeg", "png". Default: "png" **kwargs: Additional parameters Returns: List[Image.Image]: List of PIL Image objects Supported Input Formats​ All image input parameters accept: File paths (str): Path to local image file URLs (str): HTTP/HTTPS URL to image Base64 strings (str): Base64-encoded image data File-like objects (io.BytesIO): BytesIO or similar object PIL Images (Image.Image): PIL Image object Async Processing​ FLUX.2 API processes requests asynchronously. The adapters automatically: Submit the request and receive a task_id and polling_url Poll the task status endpoint until completion Return PIL Image objects when the task succeeds Raise errors if the task fails or times out (default timeout: 5 minutes) Examples​ Complete Workflow​ from tryon.api import Flux2ProAdapter, Flux2FlexAdapter# FLUX.2 [PRO] - Simple text-to-imagepro_adapter = Flux2ProAdapter()pro_images = pro_adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="A professional fashion model wearing elegant evening wear", width=1024, height=1024)pro_images[0].save("outputs/pro_result.png")# FLUX.2 [FLEX] - Advanced generationflex_adapter = Flux2FlexAdapter()flex_images = flex_adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="A stylish fashion model wearing elegant evening wear", width=1024, height=1024, guidance=8.0, steps=50, prompt_upsampling=True)flex_images[0].save("outputs/flex_result.png")# Multi-image compositioncomposition_images = pro_adapter.generate_multi_image( prompt="Combine these clothing items into a cohesive fashion outfit", images=["top.jpg", "pants.jpg", "jacket.jpg", "shoes.jpg"], width=1024, height=1024)composition_images[0].save("outputs/composition_result.png") Image Editing​ from tryon.api import Flux2FlexAdapteradapter = Flux2FlexAdapter()# Edit image with advanced controlsimages = adapter.generate_image_edit( prompt="Transform the outfit to match a vintage 1920s fashion style", input_image="model.jpg", guidance=8.0, steps=50, prompt_upsampling=True, seed=42)images[0].save("outputs/edited_result.png") Error Handling​ The adapters raise ValueError for: Missing API key Invalid parameters (e.g., guidance out of range) API errors (HTTP errors, task failures) Timeout errors (task takes too long) Invalid image formats Example: try: images = adapter.generate_text_to_image( prompt="A fashion model", guidance=15 # Invalid: must be between 1.5 and 10 )except ValueError as e: print(f"Error: {e}") Best Practices​ Prompt Quality: Write detailed, specific prompts for better results Guidance Scale: Start with default (3.5) and adjust based on results Lower (1.5-3): More creative, less strict to prompt Higher (7-10): More strict adherence to prompt Steps: More steps = higher quality but slower generation Default (28): Good balance High quality (50+): Slower but better results Seed: Use seeds for reproducible results Safety Tolerance: Adjust based on your content moderation needs Multi-Image: Use up to 8 reference images for best composition results References​ FLUX.2 [PRO] API Documentation FLUX.2 [FLEX] API Documentation FLUX.2 Overview FLUX.2 Text-to-Image Guide FLUX.2 Image Editing Guide Edit this page Previous FASHN AI Virtual Try-On Next FLUX 3 Image Overview Prerequisites Installation Quick Start FLUX.2 [PRO] - Text-to-Image FLUX.2 [FLEX] - Advanced Generation API Reference Flux2ProAdapter Flux2FlexAdapter Supported Input Formats Async Processing Examples Complete Workflow Image Editing Error Handling Best Practices References

API Reference Gemini 4 Argon (Understanding) On this page Gemini 4 Argon (Understanding) Gemini 4 and generative media​ Google’s public Gemini 4 catalog on ai.google.dev lists one stable understanding model: gemini-4-argon. It does not generate images or video (output is text only). For the usual “Gemini stack” users mean alongside Gemini 4: Task OpenTryOn registry id Google endpoint Multimodal understanding (reasoning) gemini-4-argon gemini-4-argon Image generation / edit nano-banana-2.1 (also nano-banana-2, nano-banana-2-lite) gemini-nano-banana-2.1, etc. Video generation / edit gemini-omni gemini-omni-1.2-flash (1.1 via --omni-model) Video-to-image (poster / thumbnail from a clip) uses generate --video on Nano Banana 2, 2.1, or 2 Lite via the Interactions API. See Nano Banana. Fairwind-approved defensive cyber workloads may use gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive on understand (allowlist; default thinking HIGH). Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon) is Google’s flagship reasoning multimodal model on the Gemini API (stable since Oct 2026). OpenTryOn exposes it on understand via the same GeminiUnderstandAdapter as Gemini 3.8 Flash, with Argon-specific flags. Registry id gemini-4-argon Auth GEMINI_API_KEY SDK google-genai>=2.30.1 Tier Paid (not free tier) When to use which Gemini understand model Task Model Fast, cost-efficient multimodal QA gemini-3.8-flash Hard reasoning, long outputs, agentic video on long clips gemini-4-argon CLI (multimodal)​ export GEMINI_API_KEY="..."opentryon understand --model gemini-4-argon \ --video runway.mp4 --prompt "List each look and call out fabric changes." \ --video-processing agentic --thinking-level medium --dry-run Long decode (>64K tokens)​ Multimodal (recommended): set a high --max-tokens (e.g. 131072). The adapter enables automatic_continuation on generateContent (SDK ≥2.30.1). opentryon understand --model gemini-4-argon \ --pdf spec.pdf --prompt "Extract every measurement table as JSON." \ --max-tokens 131072 --thinking-level high Text-only background job (Interactions API): --background polls a server-side interaction (up to 24h). Requires --max-tokens greater than 65536 and no --image/--video/etc. opentryon understand --model gemini-4-argon \ --prompt "Write a detailed technical spec for a sizing API." \ --max-tokens 262144 --background --thinking-level high Python​ from tryon.api.gemini import GeminiUnderstandAdapteradapter = GeminiUnderstandAdapter(model="gemini-4-argon")out = adapter.understand( video="lookbook.mp4", prompt="Summarise the collection.", video_processing="agentic", thinking_level="medium", max_tokens=131072,)print(out["text"]) MCP​ Tool: understand_gemini_4_argon. Restart MCP after upgrading OpenTryOn. API Reference Gemini 3.8 Flash (Understanding + TTS) On this page Gemini 3.8 Flash (Understanding + TTS) Two Google Gemini 3.8 models share one key (GEMINI_API_KEY, the same one used by Nano Banana, Veo and Gemini Omni): CLI model Service Model id What it does gemini-3.8-flash understand gemini-3.8-flash Text, image, video, audio and PDF in → text out gemini-3.8-flash-tts tts gemini-3.8-flash-tts Most expressive speech, 130+ languages, two-speaker dialogue gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts tts gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts Faster, lower-cost speech, 100+ languages Google-only, cloud-only: there are no open weights. export GEMINI_API_KEY="your_api_key" Understanding — gemini-3.8-flash​ Google's most capable Flash model (stable since 2 Sep 2026): 1,048,576-token context, 65,536 max output tokens. For flagship reasoning, long decode, and agentic video on long clips, use Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon). Fashion uses: attribute extraction from look photos, lookbook and runway video review, reading care labels and size charts from PDFs, voice-note briefs. opentryon understand --model gemini-3.8-flash \ --image look1.jpg look2.jpg --prompt "Compare the two outfits: garments, colours, fabrics."opentryon understand --model gemini-3.8-flash \ --video runway.mp4 --prompt "Summarise the collection and list each look's key pieces." \ --thinking-level lowopentryon understand --model gemini-3.8-flash --pdf size_chart.pdf --prompt "Extract the size table as JSON." Flag Notes --image, --video, --audio, --pdf One or more inputs each (path or URL); mix freely in one call --prompt, --system Question and optional system instruction --thinking-level low, medium or high. minimal is not supported and the API rejects it --max-tokens Output cap, at most 65,536 Inputs larger than about 18 MB go through the Files API automatically (the adapter waits until the upload is ACTIVE). YouTube links are passed straight to Gemini. gs:// and Files API URIs are used as-is. from tryon.api.gemini import GeminiUnderstandAdapterout = GeminiUnderstandAdapter().understand( image="look.jpg", prompt="List garments, colours and fabrics.", thinking_level="low",)print(out["text"], out["usage"]) Notes: thinking_level="medium" is sent as-is even if your installed google-genai predates it (the SDK's enum may not list it; the adapter silences that cosmetic warning). Planner pin: gemini 3.8 flash / gemini-3.8-flash; the understand default stays kimi-k2.6. MCP tool: understand_gemini_3_8_flash. Text-to-speech — gemini-3.8-flash-tts / gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts​ Text in, audio out. The adapter calls the Gemini Interactions endpoint (POST /v1beta/interactions) over plain REST, so it works regardless of your google-genai version (Google recommends ≥ 2.25.0 for the SDK). 30 prebuilt voices — Zephyr, Puck, Charon, Kore (default), Fenrir, Leda, Orus, Aoede, Callirrhoe, Autonoe, Enceladus, Iapetus, Umbriel, Algieba, Despina, Erinome, Algenib, Rasalgethi, Laomedeia, Achernar, Alnilam, Schedar, Gacrux, Pulcherrima, Achird, Zubenelgenubi, Vindemiatrix, Sadachbia, Sadaltager, Sulafat — plus the extended voice library and custom voice_... / voicekey_... ids from Google's voice design / replication features. Style, not stage directions. The transcript is read verbatim. Put delivery direction (emotion, pace, accent) in --style; put momentary events inline as English tags such as <sigh>, <laugh>, <short pause>, <long pause>. Output. 24 kHz mono 16-bit WAV by default. --audio-format audio/l16 (raw PCM), audio/mulaw or audio/alaw with --sample-rate 24000|16000|8000 for telephony/IVR. Two speakers per request, prebuilt voices only. For more characters, or to mix custom voices, synthesize each turn separately. opentryon tts --model gemini-3.8-flash-tts \ --text "Welcome to the spring collection <short pause> linen is back." \ --voice Puck --style "warm, upbeat, a little amused"# Two-speaker dialoguecat > turns.json <<'JSON'[ {"speaker": "Joe", "text": "Which look is your favourite?", "style": "curious"}, {"speaker": "Jane", "text": "The linen set, by far.", "style": "relaxed"}]JSONopentryon tts --model gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts \ --dialogue turns.json --speaker Joe=Puck Jane=Kore from tryon.api.gemini import GeminiTTSAdapteradapter = GeminiTTSAdapter() # gemini-3.8-flash-ttsopen("hello.wav", "wb").write(adapter.generate_speech("Have a wonderful day!", voice="Kore", style="cheerful"))open("dialogue.wav", "wb").write(adapter.generate_dialogue( [{"speaker": "Joe", "text": "Hi Jane!"}, {"speaker": "Jane", "text": "Hey Joe."}], speakers={"Joe": "Puck", "Jane": "Kore"},)) Notes: MCP tools tts_gemini_3_8_flash_tts and tts_gemini_3_8_flash_lite_tts. Planner pins: gemini tts, gemini 3.8 flash tts, gemini lite tts (a bare TTS request still defaults to eleven-v4). Compare with ElevenLabs Eleven v4, which offers cloned voices and 90+ languages. Not yet wired: the GET /v1beta/voices listing and voice design / replication endpoints (use a voice_... id you created elsewhere). API Reference FLUX 3 Video On this page FLUX 3 Video FLUX 3 Video is Black Forest Labs' unified async video endpoint: text-to-video, image keyframes, continuation from an existing clip, and a draft → enhance workflow. OpenTryOn exposes it as flux3-video on video-generate (same BFL_API_KEY as FLUX 3 Image and FLUX.2). For the Max speed/quality tier (version=max), see FLUX 3 Max (flux3-max). Prerequisites​ BFL_API_KEY=your_bfl_api_key CLI​ # Text-to-videoopentryon video-generate --model flux3-video \ --prompt "Runway walk under soft key light, camera tracking" \ --aspect-ratio 9:16 --duration 8 --resolution fhd# Image-to-video (optional end frame)opentryon video-generate --model flux3-video \ --prompt "She turns slowly toward camera" \ --image data/model-1.jpg --end-image data/model-2.jpg# Continue from an existing clipopentryon video-generate --model flux3-video \ --prompt "They step into a crowded night market" \ --video outputs/prior_clip.mp4# Draft preview, then full-quality enhance (use draft_cache URL or file from the draft result)opentryon video-generate --model flux3-video \ --prompt "Fox running through dawn mist" --draftopentryon video-generate --model flux3-video \ --draft-cache path/to/draft_cache.bin --resolution fhd# Dry-runopentryon video-generate --model flux3-video --prompt "test" --dry-run Notable flags​ Flag Default Notes --aspect-ratio auto 21:9 … 9:21 or auto --duration auto Whole seconds 5–20 (auto); v2v caps at 15 --resolution hd hd, fhd, qhd, uhd --safety-tolerance 2 0 (strictest) through 7 --draft off Fast preview; save draft_cache from the API result --no-audio audio on Silent clip --video — v2v continuation from local path or URL --draft-cache — draft_enhance from a prior draft bundle --version latest latest or max (Max is also available as --model flux3-max) Out of scope here: FLUX Video Edit at POST /v1/flux-tools/video-edit-v1 (separate BFL tool; not wired in OpenTryOn yet). API Reference Gemini Embedding 2 (Multimodal Embeddings) On this page Gemini Embedding 2 (Multimodal Embeddings) gemini-embedding-2 is Google's hosted multimodal embedding model. Text, images, audio, video and PDFs land in one shared space (100+ languages), so one index serves text-to-image, image-to-image and video/audio search. It uses the same GEMINI_API_KEY as Nano Banana, Veo and Gemini understanding. export GEMINI_API_KEY="your_api_key" Item Value CLI model gemini-embedding-2 (service embed) Adapter tryon.api.gemini.GeminiEmbeddingAdapter Output 3072-d by default; --dim 128–3072 (768 / 1536 / 3072 recommended), re-normalised Not comparable with gemini-embedding-001 (text-only, different space) or other models; re-embed if you switch Input limits​ Modality Limit Text 8,192 tokens Image PNG / JPEG, up to 6 per aggregated request Audio MP3 / WAV, up to 180 s Video MP4 / MOV, up to 120 s (≤32 sampled frames; audio track not processed) PDF 1 file, up to 6 pages Files above ~18 MB are sent through the Gemini Files API automatically. CLI​ # One vector per input, plus cosine scores against a text queryopentryon embed --model gemini-embedding-2 --image boot1.jpg boot2.jpg --query "black leather ankle boots"# "More like this": image queryopentryon embed --model gemini-embedding-2 --image catalogue/*.jpg --query-image reference.jpg# One fused vector for a product (title + photo), smaller dimensionopentryon embed --model gemini-embedding-2 --text "Linen shirt" --image shirt.jpg --aggregate --dim 768 Vectors are written to an .npz file in the output directory (emb_0, emb_1, …); the call returns its path, shapes, labels and, with a query, the scores. Flags​ Flag Meaning --text, --image, --audio, --video, --pdf Inputs (any mix) --query, --query-image Optional query; adds cosine scores (use one of the two) --task Text task prefix: search result (default), question answering, fact checking, code retrieval, classification, clustering, sentence similarity --role document (default) or query for --text items (retrieval tasks) --dim Output dimensionality, 128–3072 --aggregate Fuse all inputs into one embedding Semantics worth knowing​ Separate vs aggregated. Gemini collapses several parts in one request into a single embedding. By default OpenTryOn wraps each input separately (one vector each, batched); --aggregate sends them together. No task_type. The model ignores task types, so for text OpenTryOn adds the prompt prefix itself: queries use task: search result | query: …, documents title: none | text: …, and symmetric tasks task: clustering | query: …. Media is never prefixed, and text inside an aggregated multimodal embedding is left unprefixed (Google's guidance). Truncated dimensions are re-normalised client-side, so cosine similarity stays valid. Python​ from tryon.api.gemini import GeminiEmbeddingAdapteradapter = GeminiEmbeddingAdapter()out = adapter.embed(image=["boot1.jpg", "boot2.jpg"], query="black leather ankle boots", output_dimensionality=768)print(out["scores"]) # cosine similarity to the queryvectors = out["embeddings"] # numpy array, L2-normalised Related: the open-weight alternatives EmbeddingGemma 2 and the fashion embedders. Official docs: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings.
